Regularized (Smooth and Sparse) Principal Component Analysis for Hybrid Data

Source: R/ReMPCA.R
ReMPCA.Rd

Fits regularized principal components to a hybrid data object (functional, image, and non-functional blocks observed on a common set of rows) by a regularized power algorithm. Smoothness and sparsity can be imposed on the row direction (scores, \(u\)) and, block by block, on the column direction (loadings, \(v\)). Smoothing parameters are selected by (conditional) generalized cross-validation and sparsity parameters by \(K\)-fold cross-validation whenever more than one candidate value is supplied.

Usage

ReMPCA(
  hd,
  centerhds = TRUE,
  num_pcs = 1,
  nfolds_u = 5,
  nfolds_v = NULL,
  thresh = 1e-10,
  maxit = 100,
  tuning_iter = 1,
  parallel = FALSE,
  weights = NULL,
  smoothness_type = "Second_order",
  sparse_tuning_type = "soft",
  tuning_order = "Sparsity",
  cv.pick = "1se",
  sparse_tuning_u = NULL,
  sparse_tuning_v = NULL,
  smooth_tuning_u = NULL,
  smooth_tuning_v = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

hd

An hdClass object.

centerhds

A logical; if True, it demeans the data before calculating the principal components.

num_pcs

An integer. The number of principal components.

nfolds_u

An integer. It's used in cross validation approach for tuning the level of sparsity of rows.

nfolds_v

An integer vector of length p (the number of variables), where the i-th element specifies the number of cross-validation folds to use for the i-th variable. If not provided (NULL), a value of 5 will be assigned to all variables by default.

thresh

The convergence threshold in power algorithm.

maxit

Maximum number of iterations in power algorithm.

tuning_iter

Integer specifying the number of iterations to perform during the tuning process for conditional smoothing and sparsity parameters.

parallel

Logical; if TRUE, the cross-validation fits used to tune the sparsity parameters are distributed over a local PSOCK cluster created internally (at most 6 workers, and never more than parallel::detectCores()). The cluster is stopped before the function returns. Default is FALSE.

weights

Optional numeric vector of scaling weights. If NULL, the function automatically computes weights based on the inverse square root of the average variance of each variable. If set to 0, no scaling is applied. If a numeric vector is provided, its length must match the number of variables, and each element is used to scale the corresponding variable. This is used to adjust for scale differences across variables in the hybrid data object.

smoothness_type

A character string specifying the method used in smoothing u and/or v, must be one of "Second_order" (default), "First_order" or "Indicator".

sparse_tuning_type

A character string specifying the sparse calculation method. Must be one of "soft" (default), "hard", or "SCAD".

tuning_order

A character string representing the tuning order. If set to 'Sparsity', sparsity parameters are tuned first, followed by smoothness. If set to 'Smoothness', the order is reversed.

cv.pick

A character string specifying the rule used to select the optimal tuning parameter during cross-validation for sparsity. If set to 'min', the tuning parameter corresponding to the minimum cross-validation error is chosen. If set to '1se' (the default), the 1-standard-error rule is applied, selecting the most regularized model whose error is within one standard error of the minimum.

sparse_tuning_u

Optional. Specifies the sparsity level(s) for rows:

  • A single non-negative integer for fixed sparsity.

  • A numeric vector of candidate values, to be selected via cross-validation (CV).

  • Set to 0 for no sparsity.

  • If NULL, the function defaults to the Sparsity_parameter attribute from the hdClass object.

sparse_tuning_v

Optional. A list of length p (number of variables), where the i-th element is either a numeric value or a vector specifying candidate sparsity levels for the i-th variable. If set to NULL, the function will default to using the Sparsity_parameter_col attribute from the input object of class hdClass.

smooth_tuning_u

Optional. Specifies smoothing parameter for rows:

  • A single number for fixed smoothness.

  • A numeric vector of candidate values, to be selected via generalized cross-validation (GCV).

  • Set to 0 for no smoothness

  • If NULL, the function defaults to the Smoothing_parameter attribute from the hdClass object.

smooth_tuning_v

Optional. A list of length p (number of variables), where the i-th element is either a numeric value or a vector specifying candidate smoothing parameters for the i-th variable. If set to NULL, the function will default to using the Smoothing_parameter_col attribute from the input object of class hdClass.

verbose

Logical; if TRUE (default), progress bars and progress messages are printed. Set to FALSE for silent fitting.

Value

A list with components

ReconstructedData

List (one element per component) of the fitted rank-one matrices \(\hat u_j \hat v_j^\top\), on the centered and weighted scale.

PCFunctions

List (one element per component) of lists (one element per variable) holding the estimated loadings \(\hat v_j\).

PCScores

Matrix of scores \(\hat u_j\), one column per component.

OptimalAlphaV, OptimalAlphaU

Selected smoothing parameters, per component.

OptimalGammaV, OptimalGammaU

Selected sparsity parameters, per component.

GCVResultsV, GCVResultsU

GCV scores over the candidate smoothing parameters.

CVResultsV, CVResultsU

CV errors and standard errors over the candidate sparsity parameters.

variable_types

Type of each variable: "hd" (functional) or "rd" (regular).

VarianceExplained

Proportion of the total variation of the (centered and weighted) data explained by each estimated component, computed by projecting the data onto the span of the estimated loadings.

Details

Components are extracted sequentially. After the \(j\)-th regularized component \(\hat u_j \hat v_j^\top\) is estimated (with \(\|\hat v_j\| = 1\)), it is subtracted from the (centered and weighted) data matrix and the next component is estimated from the residual matrix.

Candidate sparsity levels are interpreted as the number of entries set to zero and should be supplied in increasing order (least sparse first), because the one-standard-error rule (cv.pick = "1se") selects the largest candidate whose CV error is within one standard error of the minimum. The cross-validation folds are formed with a fixed internal seed so that results are reproducible; the global random number generator state of the user is not modified.

References

Huang, J. Z., Shen, H. and Buja, A. (2008). Functional principal components analysis via penalized rank one approximation. Electronic Journal of Statistics, 2, 678–695. doi:10.1214/08-EJS218

Shen, H. and Huang, J. Z. (2008). Sparse principal component analysis via regularized low rank matrix approximation. Journal of Multivariate Analysis, 99(6), 1015–1034. doi:10.1016/j.jmva.2007.06.007

Huang, J. Z., Shen, H. and Buja, A. (2009). The analysis of two-way functional data using two-way regularized singular value decompositions. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 104(488), 1609–1620. doi:10.1198/jasa.2009.tm08024

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 40
u <- sin(seq(0, pi, length.out = n))
X1 <- outer(u, cos(seq(0, pi, length.out = 15))) + matrix(rnorm(n * 15, sd = 0.2), n)
X2 <- outer(u, c(1, -1, 0, 0, 0.5)) + matrix(rnorm(n * 5, sd = 0.2), n)
hd <- hdClass(list(fdClass(X1, Smoothing_parameter = c(0.01, 0.1, 1)),
                   rdClass(X2, Sparsity_parameter = 0:2)))
fit <- ReMPCA(hd, num_pcs = 1, nfolds_u = 2, nfolds_v = c(2, 2),
              cv.pick = "min", verbose = FALSE)
fit$OptimalAlphaV
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 0.01 0.00
#> 
fit$OptimalGammaV
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 0 1
#> 
plot_pc_functions(fit)
